text:
sara: quick smoke run update — spun up oak-13b-quant (8-bit asymmetric) with a two-tier prefetch + speculative mismatch fallback. Ran ~4k long-context prompts (avg 1.6k tokens). saw lower p50 latency but weird tail drift on long answers. attaching quick notes. :thinking:

jay: can you paste the config and the perf numbers? p50/p95 and token-cost delta? :eyes:

sara: perf: p50 ~ 18% down vs baseline (from 220ms->180ms per request), p95 ~ 6% down (1100ms->1034ms). token-cost estimate ~ -12% (less compute due to early accept hits). quality: automated qa-acc drop ~ 1.9% absolute (from 84.1 -> 82.2) on our instruction-qa holdout. human pairwise win-rate vs baseline: 46% (n=200).

mike: that win-rate is a bit concerning. did you run with "early_accept_threshold" tuned for model-specific calibration?

sara: default threshold (0.92) used for speed first pass. I have a second run with 0.94 queued. Also noted drift location: >1200 token prompts, the speculative prefix sometimes pulls a token that later gets overridden by the slower pass, causing trailing inconsistencies (minor hallucination in ~2% of those long ones).

lina: can you share the minimal repro (prompt + settings) so we can reproduce locally?

sara: pasted quick repro in thread:

```
# runner config snippet
model: "oak-13b-quant-8bit"
strategy:
  prefetch: two-tier
  speculative:
    workers: 2
    early_accept_threshold: 0.92
  fallback: full-kv
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  target_latency_ms: 200
```

# curl example
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"oak-13b-quant-8bit","prompt":"<long instruction + context...>","max_tokens":600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

jay: useful. can you attach the token-level trace? specifically want to see where the speculative token differs from authoritative pass and whether it's just a probability smoothing issue.

sara: attaching small excerpt inline (token probs trimmed):

"speculative sequence: ... 'the' (p=0.87) -> 'dog' (p=0.34) -> 'barked' (p=0.78)"
"authoritative: ... 'the' (p=0.63) -> 'dog' (p=0.42) -> 'barked' (p=0.81)"

mike: interesting — differences are small per-token but accumulate. sounds like prefix caching + quant noise is amplifying drift under long recursions. have we checked per-layer activations or quantization bias for early tokens?

sara: ran a quick compare of logits-variance per step: quant model has slightly higher variance at layers 10-20 for long contexts; could be 8-bit asymmetric mapping clipping mid-range logits.

lina: if that's the case, two mitigation paths: 1) raise early_accept_threshold to reduce false accepts, 2) apply lightweight calibration on logits (temperature/shift) for speculative pass. both are cheap to test.

mike: also try swapping speculative model to a fp16 variant (same architecture) as a debug — if drift disappears, it's a quant artifact not algorithmic.

sara: queued fp16 speculative run now (same seeds). expected finish ~ +40m.

jay: for eval methodology, we should run paired A/B where each prompt is served both ways and head-to-head scoring with raters blind to label. make sure we stratify by prompt length buckets (<=512, 512-1024, >1024). early signals should be per-bucket accuracy and per-token divergence.

sara: agreed. for quick triage I gave initial numbers by bucket: <=512: negligible quality change (0.3% drop), 512-1024: small drop (1.1%), >1024: larger drop (4.4%).

lina: ok that suggests warm-prefix accumulation. can we also test hybrid approach: speculative prefetch only up to 1k tokens, beyond that use normal path? should get most speedups while containing drift.

sara: tried hybrid: prefetch cap 1k -> p50 improvement ~14% (vs 18%), >1024 accuracy drop reduced to 1.2%. cost saving ~ -8% vs baseline. human win-rate bumped to 48% (n=200).

mike: promising. what's the operational risk? any extra memory or KV thrash?

sara: hybrid reduces KV thrash vs full prefetch since we avoid speculative cache for extremely long contexts. memory delta negligible. fallback rate (cases where speculative accept failed and had to reissue authoritative) ~ 6% in hybrid vs 4% in full two-tier.

jay: my recommendations for next steps:
- run fp16 speculative debug to confirm quantization culprit
- run a tuned threshold sweep (0.9/0.92/0.94/0.96) and measure cost/quality tradeoffs per length bucket
- produce a short runbook for rollout: hybrid-prefetch cap=1k, default threshold=0.94, monitor per-bucket accuracy and fallback rate, create an auto-rollback if >2% drop on >1k bucket over 1h

sara: will run the sweeps and post results. adding ticket to triage board. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary job oak-13b-quant-8bit/hybrid-prefetch-cap1k started (job id: canary-20240301-42).

mike: quick note — remember to include the eval set seed and randomization key in the ticket so we can exactly repro human eval sampling.

sara: done, ticket link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AI-3142 (private).

jay: great. ping when fp16 run completes + a short summary table.

sara: will. end."
